title: A COD customer with an old limit and a balance gets no warning or badge
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: A COD customer still has a $1,000 limit from before the release and owes $1,500.
  • You are an Admin user working at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Customer {Customer-A} holds COD, keeps a credit limit of $1,000.00 stored from before the release, has unpaid invoices totalling $1,500.00 and an open work order {Work-order-1}.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S9-05 Customer and {Work-order-1} is S2-15443.
  • Starting screen: the Work Orders page.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click "New Work Order".
  2. Pick {Customer-A} as the customer.
  3. Confirm the New Work Order window with its create button.
  4. Open {Work-order-1}.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the New Work Order window opens.
  • Step 2: the window shows {Customer-A} as the customer.
  • Step 3: no over-credit confirmation opens; the New Work Order goes straight on as for any customer.
  • Step 4: no "Over limit" badge shows.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11678 (Story 9, Over Credit warning), story SV-11680 (Story 11, Release day: what changes for existing users)

  • S9-N2: “The warning and the badge never show for a customer on COD, Due on Receipt or Credit Hold, whatever their limit or balance. A customer with a blank term counts as COD.”
  • S11-R8: “The Over Credit warning and the "Over limit" badge stop showing for customers with a $0 or blank credit limit and for customers on COD, Due on Receipt or Credit Hold (Story 9: Over Credit warning).”
  • Goals: “The Over Credit warning never appears for a customer on COD, Due on Receipt or Credit Hold, or with a $0 or blank credit limit.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

Design canvas "Default Credit Terms" (https://claude.ai/artifact/2erYxWz2ffDNcoXzEfu6wf), read 23 Oct 2026: page "8 Over Credit warning" ("COD customer, $0 limit, owes $1,200: no warning"). Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the PRD quotes.

  • “In production this same dialog also opens for a customer on COD or Due on Receipt, or with a blank or $0 limit, as soon as they owe anything.”
